lead: Operative delivery stations: ventouse and forceps on a model, and caesarean section (consent, preparation, post-operative orders, viva).
f: Prolonged 2nd stage · maternal exhaustion · fetal distress in the 2nd stage · conditions where pushing is unsafe (heart disease, severe PE)
Fully dilated, membranes ruptured · head ≤ 1/5 palpable, at or below the spines · position known · empty bladder · analgesia · consent · a place to go (theatre) if it fails

sc: Prolonged 2nd stage, head 0/5, station +2, OA → Low ventouse or forceps

f: Cup on the flexion point (3 cm in front of the posterior fontanelle, on the sagittal suture) · pull with contractions along the pelvic curve · max 3 pulls, stop after 2 detachments · not before 32 wk; care at 32–36 wk · not for a face

sc: Delivery needed in the 2nd stage at 30 wk → Forceps, not ventouse

f: Left blade first (left hand, left side) · lock without force · Wrigley (outlet, at CS) · Neville-Barnes (low, mid-cavity) · Kielland (rotation, sliding lock) · Piper (aftercoming head)
Ventouse: more failure, less maternal trauma; cephalhaematoma, chignon, retinal bleeds · forceps: more 3rd/4th degree tears; facial bruising, facial nerve palsy
Category 1: threat to life, ≤ 30 min · category 2: compromise, ≤ 75 min · 3: needs early delivery · 4: elective at 39 wk

sc: Cord prolapse at 6 cm, live baby → Category 1 CS

f: Benefits, risks (bleeding, infection, VTE, bladder or bowel injury, future praevia and accreta) · fast, antacid · group and save · cefuroxime 1.5 g before the incision · spinal preferred · left tilt 15° · oxytocin 5 IU slow IV after the baby
Lower segment: less bleeding, scar ruptures in about 0.5% · classical: very preterm, transverse lie with back down, lower-segment fibroid, perimortem; rupture 2–9%, no labour next time
Observations · fluids until drinking · analgesia · LMWH for emergency CS or risk factors · catheter out at about 12 h · early walking, feeding

tr: Ergometrine in a hypertensive woman; no thromboprophylaxis
